title: Every tuned constant in the core blend was selected against a day-to-day board-churn metric the repo's own report calls 'product-bad'; none was ever tuned against accuracy
claimUnderTest: reports/backtest_blend_params.md: 'Lower = more stable = probably better-calibrated.' Six committed reports present recommendations in the vocabulary of validation ('Promote α = 0.00', 'The design-choice justification … is empirically validated').
observed: Every backtest in reports/ optimizes mean absolute change in canonicalConsensusRank across consecutive-day pairs. Per constant: α shrinkage — stability; report recommends α=0.00, production ships 0.10, and the joint report states plainly that the stability optimum is 'use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources… That's product-bad'. MAD λ — stability; report recommends 0.0, production ships 0.0, so the one constant that matched its report is the one that switched the stage off. _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N — stability; report recommends N=400, production ships 500, and the script's own header calls the metric 'degenerate for this particular question' because a smaller N flattens more of the board and therefore has less left to churn ('a maximally uninformative board can win'). Soft fallback — stability; recommends distance=0.00. Coverage weight (MIN_FULL_COVERAGE_DEPTH=60) — no backtest of any kind exists; docs/measurements/coverage-weight-impact-2026-07-29.json measures its IMPACT after the fact, not its correctness. No accuracy target exists anywhere in this path: the repo has no forward-looking outcome join for the market board.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && grep -n 'product-bad' reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md && grep -n 'Promote' reports/alpha_shrinkage_backtest_full.md reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import src.api.data_contract as dc;print('live alpha',dc._ALPHA_SHRINKAGE,'live N',dc._PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N,'live lambda',dc._MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA)"
reproduction.expected: live constants trace to an accuracy measurement
reproduction.actual: joint report line 9 contains 'That's product-bad'; alpha report says 'Promote α = 0.00' vs live 0.1; N report says 'Promote N=400' vs live 500; every objective is mean absolute rank change

numericProof.formula: count(constants whose shipped value equals its report's recommendation)

userImpact: Every value on /rankings and every trade verdict rests on a parameter set chosen to minimize how much the board moves day to day. That objective is maximized by discarding sources, is known-degenerate for N, and is unrelated to whether a player is priced correctly. Three of five constants do not even match the recommendation their own report produced, with no note anywhere saying why.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed with the verbatim 'product-bad' quote and the per-constant shipped-vs-recommended table. Also confirms PRIOR-A09-F08 (N ships 500 against its own 400 recommendation) and PRIOR-A24-F10.

whatWorks: The scripts themselves are honest instruments and reproducible; backtest_percentile_reference_n.py in particular states its own degeneracy in the module docstring and prints it into new reports. λ=0.0 was correctly acted on and the MAD stage is genuinely inert.
rootCause: No ground-truth target for dynasty asset value exists in this repository for the market board, so stability was adopted as a proxy and then read as if it were the target.
requiredRepair: Either build a realized-outcome target for the market board (the machinery exists — src/model_registry/board_holdout.py + compute_player_season_scores already do exactly this for the adjusted-board test) and re-derive the constants, or rewrite every report to state that its recommendation is a churn preference and not evidence about the constant's value.
